column1: # scripts/mem-callsites.tsv — the inventory of RAW memory-operation call sites
# (C1 audit fix round F7, 2026-09-18; checked by scripts/check-mem-callsites in scripts/ci).
# Columns: file <TAB> enclosing declaration <TAB> raw-op <TAB> count <TAB> reason.
# The raw ops read or write a cell WITHOUT emitting an access (module docstring,
# GoLean/GoCore/Ops.lean «The memory module's access discipline»); every row is a
# recorded DECISION that gc's `-race` build performs no data access at that site,
# or that the site IS the module's own operation. A new row needs a new reason; a
# site that vanished must have its row removed (the check fails on either).
# Classes (the docstring's): EMITTING OPERATION BODY · THE PEEK/RAW WRITER ITSELF ·
# ADDRESS FORMATION · METADATA · THE MAP RMW's ENTRY PEEK · MACHINE-INTERNAL CELLS ·
# DRIVER READOUT · SYNCHRONIZATION (the registry apply EMITS its events — C1 S2c) · FRESH
# ALLOCATION · NO EXECUTION (relation premises / refusal texts) ·
# TRACER OBSERVATION (tooling). Provenance: [AGENT] fix-round worker, from the
# S2b docstring's peek list; the counts are the scanner's at the inventoried tree.

DRIVER READOUT — the pool DFS driver's result readout after termination
TRACER OBSERVATION — the choice tracer reads the channel object to name select partners in its dump (tooling; not a machine step)
TRACER OBSERVATION — the choice tracer reads the sync word to report TryLock facts in its dump (tooling; not a machine step)
DRIVER READOUT — the untrusted dedup engine's observation of a terminated node (CLI-side)

DRIVER READOUT — the enumeration spec's observation of a terminated configuration
NO EXECUTION — the relation's `initialization` premise mirrors stepFn's Store.alloc (Step is the Prop-level twin; the label is fixed by the premise)
FRESH ALLOCATION — block-scoped declaration cells (the malloc convention: the creating write precedes every escape)
SYNCHRONIZATION — the atomic op's indivisible RMW read; the apply EMITS the op's access at the cell's own path with the ATOMIC kind and its clock action (`atomicEvents`, C1 S2c)
SYNCHRONIZATION — the channel object's state read; the apply EMITS gc's channel-object accesses (`chanSendEntry`/`chanCloseWrite`) and the slot / close actions (C1 S2c)
SYNCHRONIZATION — the channel payload write of send/recv/close (channel-object traffic; the payload VALUE's data accesses are the sender's/receiver's own emitted stores)
ADDRESS FORMATION — the array-size load for the slice header's bounds (gc computes from headers and types)

FRESH ALLOCATION — append's spilled backing array, allocated in the arm's COMMIT closure (C1 S3: the validate phase read the old elements through Mem.loadSlice; the commit allocates and writes the header through Mem.store)
FRESH ALLOCATION — .allocNew / .makeSlice payload cells, allocated in the arms' COMMIT closures (C1 S3; the target store that follows is an emitting Mem.store)
FRESH ALLOCATION — makeMap / makeChan payload cells (no declared value type), allocated in the arms' COMMIT closures (C1 S3)
FRESH ALLOCATION — bytesFromString / runesFromString backing arrays
METADATA — lengthOf/capacityOf on a channel: c.qcount/c.dataqsiz are read uninstrumented in gc (probe p26, U2)
METADATA — lengthOf/capacityOf on a pointer-to-array: `len` is a constant of the type, the cell is loaded only to check the operand IS a pointer value (fail closed otherwise)
SYNCHRONIZATION — the TRY heads read the primitive's state word; `applyTryLock` EMITS the word accesses and the success-only acquire action (C1 S2c)
SYNCHRONIZATION — the .syncData state-word stores (never a data access); the apply EMITS the sync-word accesses (`syncEntryKinds`/`syncReleaseTailKinds`, U4) and the acquire/release actions (C1 S2c)
SYNCHRONIZATION — per-kind sync-word reads (Mutex/RWMutex/WaitGroup/Once)
SYNCHRONIZATION — TryLock's pre-committed state-word store; the apply EMITS the word accesses and, on success, the acquire action (C1 S2c)
SYNCHRONIZATION — the atomic op's indivisible RMW write (its access is `applyAtomicOp`'s emission with the ATOMIC kind, C1 S2c)
FRESH ALLOCATION — per-iteration loop variable cells
FRESH ALLOCATION — parameter cells at frame entry

SYNCHRONIZATION — the select commit reads the channel object's state and EMITS the committed clause's slot / close action (the poll reads are the caller's, C1 S2c)
SYNCHRONIZATION — select commit's channel payload write
ADDRESS FORMATION — the base-cell load for bounds/nil while forming the element address (resolveChain goes through it)

THE DRIVERS' PEEK ITSELF — loadMany's own recursion

SYNCHRONIZATION — TryLock's state-word read at the consult

SYNCHRONIZATION — the resumed sync op reads the state word; the wake EMITS its acquire action (no word access at a wake — BUG-080, C1 S2c)
